title: Meta: survey of Chinese/Russian/Japanese-language literature on ES (e.g. Chinese journals on 4/n)
connection: Much ES-adjacent elementary work appears in non-English journals ↔ missed identities or computations.
why: Coverage check; Yamamoto's work was in Japanese journals; Chinese elementary NT journals have many unit-fraction papers.
first_step: Search CNKI-indexed titles for 'Erdős–Straus' / '4/n' and summarise any method not in repo.

title: Universal vs per-prime certificate menus: minimal menu covering all primes in [X, 2X]
connection: Set cover over a dyadic block ↔ how menu size must grow with X (B1 says unbounded).
why: The growth law of the minimal menu (e.g. ~ log X or ~ (log X)²) is a quantitative replacement for the qualitative B1 and could be compared with the CRT-adversary cost.
first_step: Greedy set cover for primes ≡ 1 mod 24 in [10^k, 2·10^k], k = 4..8, with menu items = (u,C) pairs; fit menu size vs k.

title: Gowers' quasirandom groups: ABC = SL₂(𝔽_q) for dense A,B,C — local covering for ES₅ words
connection: Gowers (and Nikolov–Pyber) show that if |A||B||C| > |G|³/m (m = minimal nontrivial representation dimension) then ABC = G; ES₅ certificates are length-3 products of letters from fixed sets.
why: Gives a clean local (mod q) surjectivity criterion for length-3 words — the local layer of ES₅ — and quantifies how dense the letter sets must be mod q.
first_step: Compute the reductions mod q of the ES₅ letter sets A, B, C (with entries bounded by p-dependent ranges) and check the Gowers inequality for q ≤ 50.
refs: Gowers, Quasirandom groups, Combin. Probab. Comput. 17 (2008)
Nikolov–Pyber, Product decompositions of quasirandom groups and a Jordan type theorem, JEMS 13 (2011)

title: ES with large C (C up to p or p²): is the problem *easier* with a power-size reservoir, and does it still imply something?
connection: ES(p) only needs ONE C; nothing stops C from being huge. With C ≤ p^A the number of candidate C is p^A, the expected number of wins Σ_{C ≤ p^A} 1/φ(4C)·(…) ≈ A log p — still log! (Each C wins with probability ~1/φ(4C)... no wait: probability that 4Cp+1 has a divisor ≡ −1 mod 4C is roughly (number of divisors)/φ(4C) ≈ log(4Cp)/(4C)… so Σ_C log(Cp)/C ≈ log p · log X.) So count ≈ log p · log X even with X = p^A — logarithmic in X, confirming B3 for Type II. BUT in the e-slice/Type I forms, parameters (c, d) are two-dimensional: #(c,d) ≤ X² with win-probability 1/φ(4cd)·τ — Σ_{c,d ≤ X} τ(p² + 4c²d)/(4cd) ≈ log p · log²X. Still polylog. Confirms: no power reservoir in any parametrisation. Record as a calibration item.
why: Documents rigorously that every parametrisation has a polylog expected count regardless of the range; useful as a lemma for the 'generator matrix'.
first_step: Write the expected-count computation for Type I, Type II, and e-slice forms with ranges up to p^A; confirm polylog; check against ES_APPROACH_GENERATORS §B3.

title: Multiplicative energy of divisor classes vs additive shifts N_e = (p + e)/4
connection: Sum-product: sets with small multiplicative energy have large sumsets. The divisor-class multisets of N_e across consecutive windows e (an additive progression in N) — compute their multiplicative energies; ES failure across many windows would force large multiplicative structure (subgroup trapping) along an additive progression.
why: Quantitative version of the sum-product incompatibility item, measurable on data.
first_step: For hard primes, compute E^×(classes of divisors of N_e mod e) for e ≤ 10³ and compare with random integers.

title: Problem 308: Croot’s threshold for unit-fraction subset sums
connection: Problem 308 ↔ ES F01, F04, F12, F21: existence threshold, reciprocal subset sums and pointwise representation.
why: Croot’s result controls the least integer missed by subset sums of reciprocal sets; this could inform a greedy/supplementary-term strategy for ES.
first_step: Read Croot [Cr99] on the page and test whether its threshold argument can start from one ES denominator and complete with two terms.

title: Effective Oppenheim (Lindenstrauss–Margulis–Mohammadi–Shah) for indefinite ternary ES forms
connection: LMMS give effective density of values of indefinite ternary forms at integer points; the quadratic part n(xy+yz+zx) of U_n is an indefinite ternary form.
why: Effective value-distribution of the quadratic part near targets proportional to xyz may constrain solution geometry.
first_step: Write ES as Q(x,y,z) = (4/n)·xyz with Q = xy+yz+zx and see whether effective Oppenheim-type counting with a cubic weight is meaningful.
refs: Lindenstrauss–Margulis–Mohammadi–Shah, Quantitative behavior of unipotent flows and an effective avoidance principle, arXiv:1904.00290

title: Uncertainty-guided experiment allocation
connection: Allocate computation to prime strata where count models disagree rather than only to predicted hardest cases.
why: Disagreement can expose model misspecification and broaden the exploratory dataset.
first_step: Compare two simple count models and search a balanced sample of their largest disagreement cases.

title: Erdős's 'covering congruences' letters and the Erdős–Selfridge sign heuristics as hints for which modulus families to try
connection: Erdős proposed many covering-type conjectures; his letters to Selfridge (published partially) contain rules of thumb for when covering fails; a historian's reading may give the exact reason Erdős believed ES was 'not provable by congruences alone'.
first_step: Search 'Erdős Straus conjecture congruences cannot suffice Erdős remark' and read Erdős–Graham 'Old and new problems' §on unit fractions for Erdős's own assessment.
refs: Erdős–Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980)

title: Mixing of the map p ↦ (p mod 4uC−1) as u,C vary: equidistribution of residues of a single integer
connection: Residues of a fixed p modulo a growing family of moduli ↔ ES needs p ≡ −u mod (4uC−1) for some pair; this is 'one integer vs many moduli' — Erdős–Turán type discrepancy.
why: Discrepancy of {p/m} for m in a structured set is a classic (Vinogradov-type) problem; known results (e.g. on p mod m for m ≤ √p) might give existence in some ranges.
first_step: Measure discrepancy of fractional parts {(p+u)/(4uC−1)} over the trial set and compare with random; the ES event is the fractional part being exactly 0.

title: Real cyclotomic field Q(ζ_p)^+: cyclotomic units tied to p supply ES solutions; descend by trace
connection: Q(ζ_p)^+ has totally positive cyclotomic units (e.g. squares of (1 − ζ^a)/(1 − ζ) suitably normalized) and p is totally ramified. Positive ES for 4/p holds there by the unit mechanism; tracing a solution down to Q gives 2(p − 1)/p = Σ Tr(1/α_i), an Egyptian-type identity with trace numerators.
why: Provides an explicit p-indexed family of algebraic solutions whose descent might be engineered (choice of unit) to have unit-fraction traces — an algebraic source of p-dependent certificates.
first_step: For p = 5, 13, 17 compute a totally positive cyclotomic unit η ≡ −1 mod an inert-type prime and the resulting solution; compute traces of the denominators.

title: Eichler–Selberg trace formula: Hurwitz class numbers H(4p − t²) sum to traces of Hecke operators — does an ES count hide in a trace?
connection: Σ_t H(4p − t²) = (traces of T_p on cusp forms) + explicit terms (Eichler–Selberg). ES-type counts involve divisors of p² + 4c²d = discriminant-like quantities −(p² + 4c²d) = disc of forms? For Type I, 4c²d + p² ≡ p² mod 4 ≡ 1 mod 4... hmm, −(p² + 4c²d) ≡ 3 mod 4 is a valid negative discriminant! So Type I involves H(p² + 4c²d)-type class numbers summed over c — resembling Σ_t H(4n − t²) with roles of t and n changed (t ↔ p fixed, n ↔ varying c).
why: If Σ_c H(p² + 4c²d) over c in an AP equals a trace of a Hecke operator at p on some space (via a 'reversed' Eichler–Selberg), then positivity/non-vanishing of traces (Deligne bounds give |tr T_p| ≤ (dim)·2p^{(k−1)/2}; not positivity) — more usefully, the trace formula gives an *exact* identity which might convert a 'divisor in class' count into a modular-form coefficient count.
first_step: Search 'Hurwitz class numbers H(p² + 4m) sum' and 'class number sums over quadratic polynomials'; check Eichler–Selberg with weight/level to see if Σ_m H(p² + 4m) (m in an AP) is a known trace.
refs: Zagier, 'Nombres de classes et formes modulaires de poids 3/2'

title: Density of states near valid certificates
connection: Count parameter assignments by exact residual size and divisibility defect rather than only success or failure.
why: Near-zero abundance might suggest a correction lemma or reveal that approximate solutions are misleading.
first_step: Compute the joint histogram of residual numerator and gcd defect for a small parameter box.

title: Lefschetz number of a map on a 'certificate space' with ES-certificate fixed points
connection: Lefschetz fixed-point theorem: L(f) ≠ 0 ⇒ fixed point. A continuous or algebraic self-map of a compact space whose fixed points are ES certificates and whose Lefschetz number is computable would prove existence.
why: It is the classic topological existence engine; the windmill is its discrete special case. A finite-field version (Lefschetz trace for Frobenius) counts points over F_q, not integral points.
first_step: Record the attempts in invol_topological.md; look for algebraic maps on U_n's compactification whose fixed loci are positive points (e.g. the cyclic permutation composed with a birational involution).
